A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProtoT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–B support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-model training, GLUE evaluation, throughput measurements, prototype interventions, robustness tests, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds SAE/null-model interpretability comparisons and intervention perplexity measurements.

M1.justification: The prototype mixer, read/write routing, discounted prefix mean, local convolution, low-rank values, and alpha gate remain unchanged. Revised notation and the expanded explanation of semantic specialization do not establish an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu, GLUE, the same perturbation corpora/categories, and the same intervention concepts. The added SAE/null evaluations reuse the existing interpretability task and FineWeb domain rather than introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central interpretability comparison by adding LLaMA SAE features selected by activation variance or frequency and a random-sentence null baseline (Table 4; Appendix A.8). V1 compared against LLaMA attention heads only. LLaMA, Mamba, and DeltaNet remain the performance baselines.

E3.justification: The new SAE/null evaluations introduce feature-selection and random-sentence control protocols, while existing intervention tests gain sequence perplexity as a side-effect metric. The COVID table also changes its stated probability-change units from percentage points to relative percentages (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 8). Main training, GLUE, and perturbation protocols remain.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing intervention analyses to examine collateral disruption through sequence-perplexity changes (Tables 5 and 7–10), and adds a null-model check of the interpretability scoring pipeline. The intervention concepts, cross-seed case studies, architectural ablation designs, and robustness tests were already present.

E5.justification: V2 first explicitly specifies three seeds for scalability experiments (Appendix A.1) and adds interpretability score summaries with ± values (Table 4), although the ± notation is not defined. This establishes additional reporting, not an explicit increase in runs. Existing GLUE/ablation seed averaging and correlation statistics remain.

E6.justification: V2 adds SAE/null scores and intervention perplexity deltas, and revises numerous scalability, ablation, and intervention values. Table 1's 12-layer ProtoT default-context perplexity changes from 109.6 to 88.8. ProtoT/Mamba Elo changes from 1015.93/1150.78 (v1 Table 22) to 1021.24/1041.79 (v2 Table 2), retaining their ranking. GLUE and robustness results remain unchanged apart from rounding. These are reported-result revisions, not established method improvements.

T1.justification: Routing, prefix-mean, half-life, and activation-statistic mathematics remain equivalent. V2 spells out the already-used token-repetition metric as 1 minus the unique-token fraction; this is additional explanation rather than new theory. No substantive proof, assumption, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the general competitive-performance framing toward linear-compute baselines and adds an explicit claim that targeted edits cause negligible sequence-perplexity degradation. The central contribution of a linear-cost prototype architecture with interpretable concepts remains intact.

C2.justification: V2 explains specialization through averaging incompatible meanings within a channel, interprets small intervention perplexity changes as evidence of selective editing, and explicitly warns that prototype labels are approximations rather than ground truth. It also discusses misuse of editability. These extend the retained mechanism and limitation discussions.

D1.justification: V2 replaces deferred-release promises with a repository link and states that datasets, scripts, and interactive visualizations are available there. It documents SAE training on 100M tokens, a 4,096-feature dictionary, and selection of 32 features per layer; additionally, it specifies 100 test prompts and 600 judge comparisons and explains the repetition-score calculation.

R1.justification: V2 adds circuit-discovery and logit/tuned-lens references in Section 2, plus model-editing side-effect references in Appendix A.2.1, while removing the warmup reference. The original positioning against prototype methods, Slot Attention, and Perceiver remains. Numerous publication updates concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much method/appendix prose remain. V2 condenses the abstract and experimental setup, revises contribution and interpretation paragraphs, adds a results summary, and reorganizes disclosure material. The separate AI-usage and reproducibility sections disappear, with access information moved into footnotes.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Elo results move into the main text; robustness Tables 3–5 become Table 6 panels; comparison and intervention-summary tables are added; intervention tables gain perplexity columns; and new SAE/null histograms appear. LLaMA plot captions are also corrected.

improvement.justification: The SAE/null comparisons and intervention-perplexity checks strengthen the interpretability and editing evidence, while explicit limitations and access information improve transparency. The gain is limited: small perplexity changes on selected sentences do not establish broadly negligible collateral damage, and v2 Appendix A.2.1 incorrectly quotes write-mask numbers when discussing re-initialization. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the added validation.
